chemistry_identity.reaction_name: Photooxidation of Fmoc-L-methionine to Fmoc-L-methionine sulfoxide
chemistry_identity.reaction_class: Photosensitized singlet oxygen oxidation of thioether
chemistry_identity.bond_broken: S lone pair → O–O bond of ¹O₂ (perepoxide/persulfoxide intermediate collapses to sulfoxide)
source_evidence: Fmoc-methionine sulfoxide was formed in 99% yield.

residence_time_min.text: Calculation estimated τ = 0.8 min (range 0.6-1.2 min) for a 4.86 mL reactor at 0.5 mL/min total. Available reactor is fixed at 1 mL (reactor_photo_100 — only inventory option). At Q_liquid = 0.5 mL/min and Q_gas_STP = 0.5 sccm = 0.0083 mL/min, inlet/STP τ = 1.0 / 0.5083 = 1.97 min ≈ 2.0 min. This is slightly above the 1.2 min upper bound but is the minimum achievable with the 1 mL hardware constraint and pump minimum 0.01 mL/min. Analogy 1 (photoredox, 30 min) and Analogy 2 (photocatalytic C-H, 15 min) both used longer residence times for more demanding reactions — our fast singlet-O2 oxidation (99% in 5 min batch) supports shorter τ. 2 min is a conservative first experiment; reduce to 1 min by increasing Q_liquid to 1 mL/min if over-oxidation is observed.
residence_time_min.authority: scientific rationale; not an independent validation of chemistry or safety

residence_time_basis.text: Gas-liquid system (air MFC + liquid pump): O2 equivalents determined by inlet/STP MFC flow. Pressure-corrected in-channel time = τ_inlet × (P_atm / P_reactor) = 2.0 × (1/3) = 0.67 min reported as diagnostic only. Universal physics rule: residence_time_basis must be inlet/STP for all reagent-gas designs.
residence_time_basis.authority: scientific rationale; not an independent validation of chemistry or safety

residence_time_inlet_min.text: Equal to residence_time_min = 2.0 min per inlet/STP basis definition.
residence_time_inlet_min.authority: scientific rationale; not an independent validation of chemistry or safety

residence_time_in_channel_min.text: Pressure-corrected diagnostic: 2.0 min × (1 bar / 3 bar) = 0.67 min. Gas compressed to 1/3 volume at 3 bar BPR. Reported for hydrodynamic reference only.
residence_time_in_channel_min.authority: scientific rationale; not an independent validation of chemistry or safety

flow_rate_mL_min.text: Total liquid flow = 0.5 mL/min (stream A only; stream B is gas). Chosen to give ~2 min inlet/STP residence time in 1 mL reactor. Within pump_photo_liquid range (0.01-1.0 mL/min). Calculation used Q_total = 0.5 mL/min. Analogy 2 used 0.08 mL/min for 1.2 mL reactor (15 min τ) — our faster reaction allows higher flow rate.
flow_rate_mL_min.authority: scientific rationale; not an independent validation of chemistry or safety

temperature_C.text: Protocol specifies 21°C. Chemistry Plan confirms temperature_C = 21.0. Thermostat (controller_photo_thermostat) set to 21°C. Reactor allowed temperatures include 21°C. No thermal advantage needed — singlet O2 oxidation is fast at ambient temperature. Analogy 1 (25°C) and Analogy 2 (not specified) are consistent with ambient operation.
temperature_C.authority: scientific rationale; not an independent validation of chemistry or safety

BPR_bar.text: Calculation Step 8: BPR REQUIRED for gas-liquid system. Only available BPR is bpr_photo_3 at fixed 3.0 bar. Chemistry Plan: BPR maintains elevated pressure to increase dissolved O2 via Henry's law. MeCN bp = 82°C >> 21°C operating temperature, so boiling prevention is not the primary driver but gas solubility enhancement is. 3.0 bar is the only inventory option and is appropriate.
BPR_bar.authority: scientific rationale; not an independent validation of chemistry or safety

gas_flow_sccm.text: Starting point 0.5 sccm air (1:1 v/v gas:liquid at STP). MFC range 0.1-10 sccm. Calculation flags O2 transfer sufficiency = 0.19x — increase MFC to 2-5 sccm in subsequent experiments. Chemistry Plan notes gas equivalents are unresolved; 1:1 v/v is the deterministic screening starting point.

mixer_type.text: PFA T-mixer (mixer_photo_t) — only available mixer, max 2 inputs matching our 2-stream design. Chemistry Plan specifies T-mixer for Taylor flow establishment. Compatible with 1 mm ID tubing matching reactor and connector set.

chemistry_notes.text: Type II photosensitization: 4,7-diphenyl-2,1,3-benzothiadiazole absorbs 420 nm, ISC to T1, energy transfer to 3O2 generates 1O2, which oxidizes thioether sulfur of Fmoc-L-methionine to sulfoxide via persulfoxide intermediate. Key flow advantages: (1) 1 mm ID PFA coil gives ~4000 m-1 surface-to-volume ratio vs ~100 m-1 for flask, ensuring near-complete photon absorption within 0.5 mm path length; (2) Taylor flow from T-mixer dramatically increases kLa for O2 mass transfer (batch limitation identified by Chemistry Plan); (3) BPR at 3 bar increases dissolved O2 via Henry's law. Calculations flag Da = 92 (mass-transfer limited) and O2 transfer sufficiency = 0.19x — MFC flow rate should be increased stepwise (0.5 → 2 → 5 sccm) during optimization. Reactor volume is fixed at 1 mL (only available reactor). Residence time is constrained by available hardware: with 0.5 mL/min liquid and 1 mL reactor, inlet/STP apparent residence time = 1 mL / (0.5 + 0.5/1000 L equivalent) ≈ 2 min, slightly above the calculated 0.8 min target but within the 0.6-1.2 min range when accounting for the 1 mL hardware constraint. Incompatible pairs respected: air (not pure O2) used for safety with organic solvent; residence time kept short to avoid over-oxidation. Photocatalyst susceptible to slow photobleaching — monitor UV absorbance of collected fractions. Enclosure (safety_photo_enclosure) mandatory for O2-enriched organic stream + high-intensity light.
chemistry_notes.authority: scientific rationale; not an independent validation of chemistry or safety

council_selection.text: Candidate 1 wins with a combined score of 0.882 versus Candidate 2's 0.876, a margin of 0.7% — well within the 5% tiebreak threshold. Both candidates are identical in hardware (reactor_photo_100, 1.0 mm PFA, BPR 3.0 bar, 21°C) and share the same safety (0.820), fluidics (1.000), and geometry (1.000) scores; the differentiator is the domain score (0.875 vs 0.862) and chemistry score (0.870 vs 0.830), reflecting that Candidate 1's slightly higher liquid flow rate is more consistent with the class-analogy basis for this fast singlet-oxygen oxidation. The researcher objective is a practical first flow experiment, not a demonstrated optimum; Candidate 1 is selected because it offers the higher productivity proxy (750 vs 600 mg/h) at the same risk profile, making it the more informative starting screen. The 20× residence-time reduction mandate is explicitly a hypothesis: neither candidate achieves it (both achieve ~2.5× reduction), and the gap is driven by the fixed 1 mL reactor volume — the intensification target would require a reactor volume that does not exist in inventory. The two most important uncertainties a lab chemist must test are: (1) actual gas-liquid Taylor flow establishment and O₂ delivery efficiency at 3.0 bar BPR with air MFC at 5.34 sccm, since the hydraulic model is a liquid-only proxy with unresolved multiphase slip; and (2) actual conversion at τ_liquid=2.0 min, since the kinetic model is an unvalidated first-order analogy and Da_mass=91 indicates the reaction is not mass-transfer limited in the model but this has not been measured in flow. The first bench experiment should verify that stable Taylor-flow slug pattern is established visually or by pressure-trace inspection before any chemical sample is taken.
council_selection.authority: scientific rationale; not an independent validation of chemistry or safety

council_selection_justification.text: Candidate 1 (τ=2.0 min, Q_liquid=0.5 mL/min) is selected as the first screening experiment. It carries the highest combined score (0.882 vs 0.876) and achieves a 2.5× residence-time reduction relative to the 5-min batch reference within the only available 1 mL photoreactor (reactor_photo_100). The primary researcher objective is to establish a practical first flow experiment; Candidate 1 delivers marginally higher throughput (750 mg/h proxy vs 600 mg/h) at identical hardware, safety, and geometry scores. Both candidates share the same BPR (3.0 bar, the only inventory option), the same reactor, and the same unvalidated kinetic basis. The 20× intensification mandate is a hypothesis; neither candidate achieves it, and this is acknowledged — the screen is designed to measure actual gas-liquid contact, photon penetration, and conversion, not to assert intensification. Candidate 1 is selected as the more productive starting point for that measurement.
council_selection_justification.authority: scientific rationale; not an independent validation of chemistry or safety

controls.description: Use the laboratory-approved PPE and containment for every declared reagent.
Define and rehearse the emergency feed-stop sequence.
Segregate and label all process and flush waste by hazard class.
Leak- and pressure-test the assembled system before reagent introduction.
Define blockage and overpressure response without opening a pressurized line.
Cool and depressurize through the controlled outlet before opening the system.
Use the declared interlocked light enclosure when one is available; otherwise verify equivalent laboratory-approved light shielding before irradiation.
Exclude ignition sources and minimize oxygen-containing organic holdup.
Route oxygen-containing off-gas and solvent vapor to the declared compatible vent when one is available.

operating_procedure.instruction: Prepare Stream A: on a 10 mL final-volume basis, charge Fmoc-L-methionine: 1 mmol (0.1 M final); 4,7-diphenyl-2,1,3-benzothiadiazole: 0.1 mmol (0.01 M final); add acetonitrile to 10 mL total. Convert mmol to weighed/dispensed amount using the verified reagent MW, assay, and density recorded at preparation.
Prepare Stream B: connect air to the assigned MFC at 5.33636 mL/min at STP on the declared STP basis (273.15 K, 1.01325 bar; 22.414 L/mol); no liquid stock is prepared.
Assemble only the inventory-assigned process graph and verify every equipment ID and connection against the final diagram.
Prime each liquid line with its declared solvent using its assigned pump until the outlet is bubble-free; do not introduce reactive feeds during priming.
Pressure-test with compatible inert fluid to the approved operating setpoint of 3 bar and verify stable pressure before reagents.
Use the laboratory-approved PPE and containment for every declared reagent.
Define and rehearse the emergency feed-stop sequence.
Segregate and label all process and flush waste by hazard class.
Define blockage and overpressure response without opening a pressurized line.
Cool and depressurize through the controlled outlet before opening the system.
Use the declared interlocked light enclosure when one is available; otherwise verify equivalent laboratory-approved light shielding before irradiation.
Exclude ignition sources and minimize oxygen-containing organic holdup.
Route oxygen-containing off-gas and solvent vapor to the declared compatible vent when one is available.
Start liquid feeds at the canonical setpoints. Admit gas only after liquid flow, temperature, pressure, purge, and vent checks are stable.

Allow an initial commissioning interval of at least 6 min, based on three nominal liquid-volume turnovers. Confirm steady outlet composition and stable flow, pressure and temperature before collection; elapsed time alone does not establish steady state. Measure phase holdup or tracer response when gas or a packed bed is present.

After measured steady state, collect a timed fraction over at least 2 min as an initial sampling interval; record exact start/end times and collected mass or volume. Extend collection if needed for the analytical method.

Collect the crude outlet in the assigned vessel and retain a labeled aliquot for conversion, selectivity, and yield analysis. This first screen ends at crude collection; no isolation work-up is authorized unless the chemist adds a confirmed downstream procedure to the intake package.
Stop reactive feeds, flush each compatible line, cool the reactor to a safe handling temperature, and isolate energy sources.

validation_experiments.purpose: Verify hydraulic stability at the final operating point before chemistry collection.
validation_experiments.procedure: Run compatible blank solvent at Q=0.5 mL/min, T=21.0 C, and BPR=3 bar for at least 10 min; record flow, temperature, pressure, leaks, and blockage indicators.

validation_experiments.purpose: Measure the residence-time distribution and phase holdup at the operating point.
validation_experiments.procedure: Introduce a compatible nonreactive tracer at Q=0.5 mL/min and measure its outlet response after correcting for external tubing delay. Report the measured mean, dispersion and liquid holdup separately from the calculated 0.17134 min index (inlet/STP apparent residence time); do not require agreement with an STP turnover index.

validation_experiments.purpose: Generate the first wet-lab response at the exact canonical design point.
validation_experiments.procedure: Execute the canonical operating procedure once and report conversion, isolated yield, selectivity, pressure trace, temperature trace, and any phase or blockage observations.

intensification.basis: Predicted screening target: 20.0x residence-time reduction; this is a hypothesis unless the run explicitly selects the intensify policy. Identified batch limitations: mass_transfer_gas_liquid, photon_penetration. Primary flow advantage: mass_transfer. Mechanisms: gas-liquid kLa enhancement (segmented flow), photon penetration via small ID, selectivity-sensitive stream logic. Limitation-driven IF (20x) exceeds class default (6x).
